CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C serology

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents following discovery of positive hepatitis C antibody on routine physical examination. Patient reports feeling well and was surprised by this finding. Denies prior diagnosis of hepatitis C. Reports past history of intravenous drug use but has been clean for over 15 years. Currently drinks beer daily but notes this is less than before. Smokes one to two cigarettes per day, having significantly reduced from prior consumption. Patient is married with children. Denies other significant medical conditions besides this positive finding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No medical conditions reported other than the positive hepatitis C serology.

MEDICATIONS
Not taking any medications.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes, and depression

SOCIAL HISTORY
Tobacco: Smokes one to two cigarettes per day, significantly decreased from prior use. Alcohol: Beer, daily consumption but less than previously. Illicit drugs: Past history of intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Family: Married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Within normal limits. General: Well-appearing, no distress, no jaundice. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Respiratory: Lungs clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: Bowel sounds present, soft, splenomegaly noted. Neurological/Musculoskeletal: No gait disturbance, no edema.

RESULTS
Hepatitis C antibody: Positive. Liver function panel: AST 39 (elevated), ALT within normal limits, albumin within normal limits, total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C. Patient newly diagnosed with hepatitis C based on positive antibody test. Infection likely present for several years though typically remains asymptomatic until advanced disease. Plan: Confirm diagnosis with HCV RNA testing and HCV genotype; assess severity of liver disease with ultrasound elastography to evaluate for fibrosis; screen family members (wife and children) with hepatitis C antibody testing and assist with setting up screening appointments through primary care physician; return in three weeks for follow-up and review of results; counsel on smoking cessation with consideration for pharmacologic support if not already prescribed by PCP.
